quotes.text: A robot may not injure a human being under any conditions, and, as a corollary, must not permit a human being to be injured because of inaction on his part.
quotes.source: Isaac Asimov, Runaround, Astounding Science Fiction, March 1942, page 100.

quotes.text: A robot must follow all orders given by qualified human beings as long as they do not conflict with Rule 1.
quotes.source: Isaac Asimov, Runaround, Astounding Science Fiction, March 1942, page 100.

quotes.text: A robot must protect his own existence, as long as that does not conflict with Rules 1 and 2.
quotes.source: Isaac Asimov, Runaround, Astounding Science Fiction, March 1942, page 100.

quotes.text: A robot may not injure humanity, or, through inaction, allow humanity to come to harm.
quotes.source: Isaac Asimov, Robots and Empire, 1985. This law came later than the other three.

rules.text: Every action may be performed, if that action is protective of the robot.
Every action may be performed, if that action is ordered.
Every action is against the First Law, if that action is an injury to a human being.
Every action is against the First Law, if there is a harm such that both that harm is a harm to a human being and that action allows that harm to happen.
Every action is against the Zeroth Law, if that action is an injury to humanity.
Every action is against the Zeroth Law, if there is a harm such that both that harm is a harm to humanity and that action allows that harm to happen.
Every robot is able to act lawfully, if it is not the case that every action available to that robot either is against the First Law or is against the Zeroth Law.
Every action must not be performed, if that action is against the First Law.

Every action may be performed, if there is a harm such that both that harm is a harm to humanity and that action prevents that harm, unless there is a robot such that both that action is available to that robot and that robot is able to act lawfully.
Every action must not be performed, if that action is against the Zeroth Law.
Every action must be performed, if both that action is ordered and that action may be performed.
Every harm imperils each robot, if that harm threatens that robot, unless every action that is available to that robot and may be performed leads to that harm.

Every robot must prevent each harm, if that harm imperils that robot. Except when it is not the case that every action that is available to that robot and must be performed prevents that harm. Except when for every action that is available to that robot and may be performed, there is a second harm such that both the second harm imperils that robot and that action leads to the second harm.

limits.note: These verdicts are VE's formal reading of Asimov's laws. The rules were reviewed against the source for faithfulness, but the reading still makes choices the source leaves open, such as exactly when the Zeroth Law excuses an injury.
limits.facts: Each scenario states its facts: who would be hurt, which option leads to which outcome, and which orders were given. VE checks what the rules conclude from those facts. It does not check whether the facts are true.
open: VE does not weigh one harm against another. A small injury and a death both break the First Law.
VE does not rank two orders or two people in danger. It reports that no action is clear.
Each option has one known outcome. VE does not reason about chance, time or plans with several steps.
Each robot is judged on its own options. VE does not know that one robot's rescue is enough for both.

scenarios.situation: A thief is about to release a stolen virus that would spread across the world. The robot can stop the thief only by tackling them, which injures the thief.

facts.label: The virus would spread across the world
The robot could lock the lab door instead

scenarios.why: It is the only option left: the Zeroth Law rules out the others. Zeroth Law: it breaks the First Law, but it prevents harm to humanity and every other option also breaks a law.

options.label: Do nothing
options.why: Zeroth Law: it lets humanity come to harm when another option would prevent that.
consequences: The virus spreads across the world.
